title: Crypto weakens as payment infrastructure expands and ARC weighs on the portfolio
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded around $81,460, down 1.0% over 24 hours, while ether fell 1.5% to about $2,430. CoinGecko’s total crypto market capitalization declined 4.1%, showing broader weakness beyond the two largest assets. The market is entering the weekend under pressure, with the latest rebound failing to produce a sustained recovery across crypto.

The macro backdrop also deteriorated. The Nasdaq finished its latest session down 2.15%, and the VIX volatility index rose 22%. WTI crude reached roughly $102 a barrel during the selloff, while the 10-year Treasury yield traded above 5.1%. Bitcoin weakened alongside stocks. Higher energy costs and expensive borrowing are a difficult combination for risk assets, although those simultaneous moves do not establish a single cause for crypto’s decline.

Marqeta and Coinbase announced an expanded partnership for cards funded with stablecoins. Coinbase is set to handle custody and conversion into conventional currency, Base will provide blockchain settlement, and Marqeta will handle card issuance and processing. Businesses would be able to fund card programs around the clock, with customers spending through existing merchant card networks. The practical benefit is a simpler route from a stablecoin balance to purchases. Adoption and transaction volumes will determine its commercial significance.

Bank deposit infrastructure is moving too. Jack Henry announced plans to integrate Google Cloud Universal Ledger so banks and credit unions can offer tokenized deposits. The proposed integration supports programmable payments and settlement at any hour, while helping institutions retain deposit relationships. This could bring digital asset capabilities to smaller banks through technology they already use. It remains an announced integration, with actual customer deployment still the measure of progress.

Our on-chain portfolio is about $82,800: $11,400 in the active treasury and $71,400 in the cold-storage Safe. That is $38,200, or 31.6%, below the previous update. The largest contribution is the Safe’s directly held ARC, now worth $56,900 versus $91,100, with its 26.74 million-token balance unchanged. That holding alone accounts for roughly 69% of the portfolio, before additional ARC exposure in liquidity pools. Concentration remains the main portfolio risk.

The Safe’s largest liquidity position is an $11,200 WETH/ARC pool on Aerodrome. The treasury has about $3,500 in Beefy positions spanning WETH/AERO, stablecoins and other paired assets, plus $2,500 in directly held cbETH. These provide other exposures, but are small compared with the ARC holding.

Visible lending debt totals about $4,200. Aave health factors are 2.51 in the treasury and 2.00 in the Safe. Fluid has roughly $1,060 of debt against $1,213 of supplied assets; its $153 net position has the tightest lending margin, with a health factor of 1.03.
